questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 11/2 completed? What were the results, and how should the evening confusion be followed up?
Does the combination of the 9/25 fall, unsteady gait, evening confusion and the stove incident call for a reassessment of home safety, and when should it happen?
Have the walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars been put in place, and how is PT progressing?
What respite and evening support can be arranged for Robert, and how soon?
Two withheld chart-correction notes (n015, n016) claim the 9/25 fall was charted in error, but the RN note and the PT evaluation both document it. Can HIM or the authors review and reconcile them?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window, including ED visits, urgent care, and hospital admissions, with reasons; note especially any chest pain, cardiac, or migraine-related presentations given new ischemic heart disease onset 2026-06-30.

Review cardiac follow-up since the ischemic heart disease diagnosis (2026-06-30): cardiology visits, any repeat testing, and whether the team has documented chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, and any symptoms that would prompt urgent action.

Medication reconciliation: confirm metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, nitroglycerin spray, and alendronic acid are still active and taken as prescribed; check for any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window; check adherence and refill gaps, especially for the antiplatelet and beta-blocker started 2026-07-07.
Bleeding and bleeding-risk review on clopidogrel: any reported bruising, GI bleeding, melena, hematuria, falls with head strike, or ED visits for bleeding; check recent hemoglobin or CBC if on file.
Heart-rate and blood-pressure trend on metoprolol: review resting BP and HR readings, dizziness or orthostatic symptoms, and any falls, since the beta-blocker start.

Substance use review given dependent drug abuse (onset 2018): any documented opioid or other substance use, relapse signals, pharmacy or prescriber flags, naloxone availability if relevant, and whether any controlled or pain medications were added or stopped (none appear on the active list, so confirm this is accurate and check for non-listed sources).

Chronic pain and migraine review: frequency and severity of migraine episodes, headache-related ED visits, pain scores, and any analgesic or migraine-preventive changes; note that no migraine or pain medications appear on the active list, so verify this against the full record.

Bone health and fall risk given osteoporosis (2023) and scoliosis: any fractures, falls, or near-falls in the window; alendronic acid adherence and whether the patient can take it correctly (upright 30 minutes, fasting); check for dental issues, since alendronate and impacted molars together warrant a dental-status check, and review any dental extractions or procedures.

Weight and BMI trend (BMI 30+ on record): recorded weights in the window and trend, dietary or activity-related goals, and any new cardiometabolic markers (lipids, glucose) that are due given statin therapy.

Function, ADLs and mobility, cognition, mood and attendance: changes in ADL/IADL status, mobility aids, mood screening scores, cognitive screening, and attendance at PACE day center or scheduled visits in the window; also check for any caregiver or living-situation changes, transportation issues, and caregiver strain. Care-plan items due in the window (reassessments, goal reviews, and any overdue referrals) should be listed for the IDT to address.
